title: Unità 5 · La scuola italiana
question: How does school work in Italy, and what do students do there?
workingOn: school in Italy and what we do there: -are verbs
canDo: I can say what I and other people study, eat and listen to at school.
I can say the ages and years of each school stage in Italy.
I can name the three kinds of Italian high school and the final exam.
I can ask and answer questions about my school day.
culture: In Italy, school is required from age 6 to 16, and many students stay until 19. High school lasts five years and ends with a big exam called la maturità. A ministry decides for all the schools, and each school has a preside, the principal.

grammar.head: -are verbs, all six persons: studio, studi, studia, studiamo, studiate, studiano
tricks: Cut -are, then add: io -o · tu -i · lui/lei -a · noi -iamo · voi -ate · loro -ano.
Verbs that end in -iare (studiare, mangiare) keep one i: studio, mangio; tu studi, mangi (not studii).
Loro adds -ano to the stem: parlano, ascoltano. Gli studenti = loro.
Parlare is the model for all the regular -are verbs: ascoltare, comprare, abitare.

sentences: Io studio italiano a scuola.
I study Italian at school.
Tu parli italiano con il professore.
You speak Italian with the teacher.
Marco mangia un panino a ricreazione.
Marco eats a sandwich at the break.
Noi studiamo la storia e le scienze.
We study history and science.
Voi parlate con il preside.
You all speak with the principal.
Gli studenti ascoltano il professore.
The students listen to the teacher.
In Italia la scuola superiore dura cinque anni.
In Italy high school lasts five years.
Ci sono tre tipi di scuola superiore.
There are three kinds of high school.
Il ministero decide per le scuole.
The ministry decides for the schools.
Dopo la maturità, gli studenti hanno il diploma.
After the maturità, students get the diploma.
Sono le otto: la scuola comincia.
It is eight: school starts.
Compro un panino e studio in classe.
I buy a sandwich and I study in class.

forms.why: io → -o: studio (the i stays from studi-).

trick: Parli italiano? = Do you speak Italian?
-iare verbs keep one i: studi, mangi.

read.title: Una giornata a scuola in Italia
passage: Sofia ha quindici anni e studia in un liceo.
Sofia is fifteen and studies in a liceo.
Il liceo dura cinque anni e Sofia studia l'italiano, la storia e le scienze.
The liceo lasts five years and Sofia studies Italian, history and science.
Sono le dieci: c'è la ricreazione. Sofia mangia un panino con le amiche.
It is ten: there is a break. Sofia eats a sandwich with her friends.
Dopo cinque anni c'è la maturità. Poi gli studenti hanno il diploma.
After five years there is the maturità. Then the students get the diploma.

lines: Hi Marco! What do you study?
Studio l'italiano, la storia e le scienze. E tu?
I study Italian, history and science. And you?
Io studio la matematica e l'arte. Sono le dieci!
I study math and art. It is ten!
C'è la ricreazione! Mangi un panino?
There is the break! Do you eat a sandwich?

finish: Now I know how to talk about school in Italy and about what I do at school!

idiom.en: good luck (literally: in the wolf's mouth)
idiom.ex: Oggi c'è la maturità. In bocca al lupo!
idiom.exEn: Today is the maturità. Good luck!
idiom.note: Italians say it before an exam or a big moment. The answer is Crepi! (may it die).

flags: The district guide lists only four Italian 2 units. Unit 5 is a supplemental unit, not a guide unit. Decide where it sits in your pacing.
It is the Italian 2 step up from Italian 1 Unit 5: the same school facts, but with all six forms of regular -are verbs (studiare, parlare, mangiare, ascoltare, comprare).
Regular -are verbs are on your Italian 2 midterm. The game practices only io and tu for -are verbs elsewhere, so this unit also practices noi, voi and loro.
Present tense only. No combined prepositions. The idiom In bocca al lupo! contains al, kept as a set phrase (Assunta says keep).
Chunks to confirm are known: dura, comincia, decide, si chiama, ci sono, c'è, dopo, con, poi, quanti anni.

Facts checked against Eurydice, Istat and the Italian ministry: stages 6-11, 11-14, 14-19; school required from 6 to 16; five-year high school; maturità; ministry called MIM. The Crepi! reply is general knowledge (Unverified).
Everything is Untested and all the Italian needs your review.
